title: Derived-functor criterion and comparison maps in finitely many variables
statement:
Fix $1\le n\le4$. For $1\le i\le n$ let $A_i$ be a category [def-nagata-category], $W_i$ a class of arrows containing identities, $L_i:A_i\to D_i$ a localization, and $P_i\subseteq A_i$ a full subcategory whose inclusion is a left derivability structure [def-sfb-left-derivability-structure]. The product inclusion $\prod_iP_i\to\prod_iA_i$ is a left derivability structure for the product arrow class consisting of tuples $(w_i)_i$ with $w_i\in W_i$ for every $i$, and $L=\prod_iL_i$ is a localization of that class. The full subcategory $P_i=A_i$ with identity inclusion is permitted and is a left derivability structure. Let $H$ be any category and $F:\prod_iA_i\to H$ a functor whose restriction to $\prod_iP_i$ sends each coordinate $W_i$-arrow to an isomorphism when the other coordinates lie in their $P_j$. Then there exist $LF:\prod_iD_i\to H$ and $\varepsilon:LF\circ L\Rightarrow F$ that are a total left derived functor in all $n$ variables: for every $V:\prod_iD_i\to H$, composition with $\varepsilon$ gives a bijection
$$ \operatorname{Nat}(V,LF)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Nat}(V\circ L,F). $$
For a candidate $(T,\eta:T\circ L\Rightarrow F)$, this universal property holds if and only if every $\eta_{(P_1,\ldots,P_n)}$ is an isomorphism. In particular the counit of $LF$ is invertible there. If $G$ satisfies the same hypotheses with chosen $(LG,\varepsilon_G)$ and $\tau:F\Rightarrow G$, there is a unique $L\tau:LF\Rightarrow LG$ with
$$ (\varepsilon_G)_x\circ(L\tau)_{Lx}=\tau_x\circ\varepsilon_x $$
for every tuple $x$ of objects of the $A_i$. This operation preserves identities and composition and sends natural isomorphisms to natural isomorphisms. For arbitrary $V$, maps $\gamma_1,\gamma_2:V\Rightarrow LF$ are equal if $\varepsilon\circ(\gamma_1 L)=\varepsilon\circ(\gamma_2 L)$. More generally, natural transformations between any two functors on $\prod_iD_i$ are determined by their components at tuples $(L_1P_1,\ldots,L_nP_n)$.
